sentences.text: ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Sanjay Bishnoi  Mr. Deepak Saraswat For Respondent(s) : Mr. Narendra Gehlot, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 06/12/2025 1.

This bail application under Section 483 BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.178/2023, registered at Police Station Sadar Barmer,
District Barmer, for offences under Sections 8/15 & 25 of NDPS Act; Sections 3/25 of Arms Act; and Sections 420 and 465 of IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per the prosecution, in the intervening night of 25.05.2023, the SHO, P.S. Sadar Barmer recovered a huge quantity of the contraband (Poppy Husk/Straw) from three vehicles viz. Eicher Truck bearing registration No. RJ-04-GC-1673,
unnumbered Scorpio and Isuzi.

Learned counsel submitted that the allegation against the present petitioner is that he is the registered owner of the Isuzi vehicle having Registration No.
RJ-04-GC-3332 which was being used by (Uploaded on 06/12/2025 at 04:39:55 PM)
[2025:RJ-JD:52976] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-8476/2025] the co-accused persons and the petitioner for transporting the huge quantity of the recovered contraband.

sentences.text:
Drawing attention of this Court towards the challan papers, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as a matter of fact, the offending vehicle, i.e., Isuzi vehicle having Registration No.
RJ-04-GC-3332 was already sold by the petitioner through an agreement to sale dated 25.04.2023 to one Manohar Lal.
Learned counsel submitted that there is nothing on record to show that after the offending vehicle being sold by the petitioner to Manohar Lal, the same was still used by the petitioner.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner has been implicated in the present case solely on the basis of suspicion without there being any cogent evidence available on record indicating his role in commission of the alleged crime.

4. Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody; the co-accused persons namely Babu Lal (S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 3382/2025),
Hanuman Ram (S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 2/2025), and Kojaram (S.B.
Criminal Miscellaneous 2nd Bail Application No. 6491/2024) have already been enlarged on bail by this Court as well as the co-ordinate Bench of this Court; and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused- petitioner.
5. Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the petitioner is the registered owner of the offending vehicle and therefore, it (Uploaded on 06/12/2025 at 04:39:55 PM) [2025

Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that sufficient material is available on record to establish the active role of the petitioner in commission of the alleged crime.

Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the petitioner is a habitual offender and he is facing criminal trial in more than four cases of similar nature, therefore,
looking to the seriousness of the allegations levelled against him, he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
6. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

7. Having considered the rival submissions, facts, and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that in the present case, the contraband greater than the commercial quantity was not recovered from the conscious possession of the present petitioner; the documents available on record indicate that the Isuzi vehicle having Registration No. RJ-04-GC-3332 was already sold and handed over by the petitioner to one Manohar Lal through an agreement to sale and the co-accused persons have already been enlarged on bail.

Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
8.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Prakash Choudhary S/o Shri Rugaram, arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.178/2023, registered at Police Station Sadar Barmer, District Barmer, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in

[CRLMB-8476/2025] any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- and two sureties of Rs.50,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, for his appearance before that Court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the Prakash Choudhary vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:52976) on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55194387/
